A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GTPO and GRPO-S through Dynamic Entropy Weighting. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v5 reports original Qwen2.5 experiments on AIME 2024/2025, training trajectories, hyperparameter sensitivity results and a qualitative case study.

after.justification: v6 retains original experimental results and supplementary analyses and adds MATH 500 results, another model–benchmark configuration and comparator results.

M1.justification: The core algorithms remain, but geometric reward normalizers are corrected to use group and active-sequence counts instead of response lengths. Algorithm 1 now specifies arithmetic importance weighting, while geometric weighting remains an alternative in Appendix C. These are changes to the written procedure; rerunning retained experiments is not established.

E1.justification: v6 adds MATH 500 evaluation for both model sizes while retaining AIME 2024/2025. This extends benchmark coverage within mathematical reasoning without adding another task type or domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds DAPO w/ Forking Tokens as an evaluated comparator, including in retained AIME settings. GRPO and DAPO remain; comparator membership in the existing trajectory and sensitivity analyses is unchanged.

E3.justification: v6 adds the Qwen2.5-7B/AIME 2024 experimental configuration. The shared metric definitions, batch/group sizes, learning rate, sampling parameters and length limits remain unchanged. Explicitly mentioning the existing overlong penalty does not establish that it was newly enabled.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter sensitivity analysis is retained as Figure 5 instead of Figure 3. Entropy rebound, response length, clipping, reward-trajectory analyses and the qualitative case study are retained in renumbered appendices. The newly numbered entropy-comparison diagram was already present.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, independent repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing smoothed trajectories and their displayed bands are retained without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially expands results with MATH 500, AIME 2024 on 7B and Forking Tokens comparisons. For example, new 32B MATH 500 Mean@32 scores are 85.72 for GTPO, 85.79 for GRPO-S and 85.21 for Forking Tokens. Shared AIME scores match after percentage conversion. Exact Pass@2/8/16 entries and APG/RPG rows are removed, although the existing trajectory plots remain.

T1.justification: Section 2.4 and Appendices B.3–B.4 replace approximate-gradient and local-optimum arguments with formal reward-conservation propositions, conditional asymptotic-consistency proofs and theorems claiming a shared global optimum. Entropy-consolidation and bounded-score assumptions materially revise the guarantees. The basic variance calculations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract extends empirical superiority claims to MATH 500 and entropy-guided competitors and emphasizes GRPO-S stability. The introduction recasts the theoretical contribution from variance-reduction motivation to unbiasedness and convergence. The central contributions of entropy-based token and sequence reward shaping remain.

C2.justification: v6 adds a GRPO length-bias explanation, acknowledges bias from geometric averaging, and explicitly describes token independence as a simplifying assumption despite autoregressive generation. The AIME 2025 plateau explanation in v5 Table 1 is removed. Existing entropy-rebound and implicit-curriculum interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v6 adds numerical-stability safeguards and absent-token handling, explicitly states use of the previously documented overlong penalty, and mentions reward/advantage clipping in Appendix B.4. Conversely, Table 1 no longer identifies its scores as maxima. These documentation changes do not establish changed experimental execution.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially redirects positioning toward continuous reward redistribution versus entropy regularization and binary token selection. Wang et al.'s 80/20 work was already cited in v5, but becomes a direct methodological contrast and evaluated competitor. Process-supervision and agent-RL references are added while several broader introductory references are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial introductory passages are rewritten, Algorithm 1 becomes numbered stages, and the theoretical narrative is reorganized around propositions and proofs. Geometric definitions move into a dedicated appendix. Much of the discussion and supplementary-analysis prose remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text switches to two columns, Figures 1–2 are extensively redrawn, and Table 1 is reorganized into benchmark columns and model blocks with revised highlighting. The existing entropy-comparison matrix becomes Figure 4, and retained plots and case-study boxes are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The added entropy-guided comparator and MATH 500 results strengthen empirical support, and explicit assumptions improve transparency. However, Theorems 2.4/B.7 strengthen v5's local-optimum argument to a shared global optimum that conditional asymptotic agreement of positive-reward gradients does not establish. Removal of the maximum-score disclosure also reduces reporting clarity. These empirical gains and theoretical/reporting drawbacks leave the net quality direction uncertain.
